Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency; electronic headquarters (Sede Electrónica): https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Tax census and VAT registration are managed through Modelo 036 (general registration) or Modelo 037 (simplified registration); customs and export formalities are handled by the AEAT Customs Department (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales).

E-government filing portal

Step 1: A Spanish-resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is incorporated by public deed before a notary and registered in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); AEAT assigns a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) before the deed is formalized, followed by the definitive corporate NIF with the 'B' prefix (B + 7 digits + control character). Step 2: A foreign non-resident entity that performs taxable activities in Spain, such as maintaining local warehousing or making taxable supplies, must register in the Economic Activities Census by filing Modelo 036 before commencing operations. AEAT assigns the NIF applicable to the foreign entity's category: an 'N'-prefixed NIF where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment, or the permanent-establishment NIF where a Spanish branch or fixed place of business is created. Step 3: The foreign entity must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain when AEAT requires one for VAT compliance, and must obtain the Spanish VAT identification number, consisting of the NIF prefixed with 'ES' (e.g., ES + NIF), for intra-Community transactions and VIES registration. Step 4: Supporting documents normally requested by AEAT include: certificate of incorporation and registry extract from the home jurisdiction, evidence of foreign tax residence, copy of the public deed and tax representative appointment, power of attorney, and a description of the Spanish fixed establishment or storage operation. Filing is performed electronically using a recognised digital certificate (DNIe, FNMT, or an accepted qualified e-certificate).

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxable person under Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Law 27/2014) and is taxed on its worldwide income at the general rate of 25%. The SL is not eligible for pass-through treatment or US-style check-the-box classification; fiscal classification follows the Spanish civil and commercial legal form. Income of a foreign permanent establishment of the SL may be exempt under Article 22 LIS when the foreign branch is subject to a comparable corporate tax of at least 15%; otherwise a foreign tax credit applies. Dividends and interest paid by the SL to non-resident shareholders are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax (IRNR) at the applicable treaty or statutory rate. — Step 1: A Spanish-resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is incorporated by public deed before a notary and registered in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); AEAT assigns a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) before the deed is formalized, followed by the definitive corporate NIF with the 'B' prefix (B + 7 digits + control character). Step 2: A foreign non-resident entity that performs taxable activities in Spain, such as maintaining local warehousing or making taxable supplies, must register in the Economic Activities Census by filing Modelo 036 before commencing operations. AEAT assigns the NIF applicable to the foreign entity's category: an 'N'-prefixed NIF where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment, or the permanent-establishment NIF where a Spanish branch or fixed place of business is created. Step 3: The foreign entity must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain when AEAT requires one for VAT compliance, and must obtain the Spanish VAT identification number, consisting of the NIF prefixed with 'ES' (e.g., ES + NIF), for intra-Community transactions and VIES registration. Step 4: Supporting documents normally requested by AEAT include: certificate of incorporation and registry extract from the home jurisdiction, evidence of foreign tax residence, copy of the public deed and tax representative appointment, power of attorney, and a description of the Spanish fixed establishment or storage operation. Filing is performed electronically using a recognised digital certificate (DNIe, FNMT, or an accepted qualified e-certificate).

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation - the Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxable person under Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Law 27/2014) and is taxed on its worldwide income at the general rate of 25%. The SL is not eligible for pass-through treatment or US-style check-the-box classification; fiscal classification follows the Spanish civil and commercial legal form. Income of a foreign permanent establishment of the SL may be exempt under Article 22 LIS when the foreign branch is subject to a comparable corporate tax of at least 15%; otherwise a foreign tax credit applies. Dividends and interest paid by the SL to non-resident shareholders are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax (IRNR) at the applicable treaty or statutory rate.

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a check-the-box regime for commercial companies; classification is mandatory and follows legal form. Available statutory elections relevant to this exporting SL: (a) consolidated corporate income tax group election under Article 64 LIS, available to a Spanish parent and its resident subsidiaries where control is at least 75%; (b) VAT group registration (régimen especial del grupo de entidades) for integrated structures with control above 50%; (c) voluntary enrolment in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time VAT bookkeeping system by enterprises below the EUR 24 million mandatory threshold; and (d) mandatory anti-hybrid alignment under the ATAD transposition, under which the Spanish legal form governs the entity's fiscal character and no elective mismatch mechanisms are available for a resident SL.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

There is no general turnover exemption threshold in the Spanish VAT general regime: any person or entity carrying out business or professional activities must obtain VAT census registration through Modelo 036 before commencing the activity, irrespective of turnover. The Spanish simplified regime (régimen simplificado), applicable only to enumerated small business sectors with prior-year taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000, does not cover wholesale trading of processed dehydrated vegetable products. The EU-based threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year is relevant solely for intra-Community distance sales of goods and works through the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) when exceeded; this exporter's B2B export model falls outside that threshold framework. Statistical Intrastat thresholds for dispatches of goods to other Member States are updated annually by AEAT and apply when the exporter's intra-EU dispatches exceed the published amount.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rating (export exemption with right to deduct input VAT) applies under Article 21(2) of Ley 37/1992 to supplies of dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper physically dispatched or transported by the seller, or for the seller's account, to a destination outside the EU customs territory. The substantive conditions are: (i) the goods must leave the EU within the period evidenced by the customs export declaration; (ii) the exporter must hold the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) endorsed by the customs office, the transport document, and proof of payment; (iii) the supply must be made under the exporter's Spanish VAT registration; and (iv) the buyer must be a person established outside the EU or export must be effectuated through an indirect-export arrangement. Ancillary services directly related to the exported goods (freight, handling, storage, inspection) supplied to a third-country customer may also be zero-rated under Article 21(4) and (5) LIVA, and pure B2B services located to a non-EU customer are outside the Spanish VAT net under Article 70 LIVA. The zero-rating applies irrespective of the Incoterms used, provided the transport documentation demonstrates a non-EU destination.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA / EX-A Documento Único Administrativo) electronically accepted by Spanish Customs, with the correct TARIC tariff line for dehydrated vegetables or crushed/powdered pepper
  • Commercial invoice and packing list (Spanish/English) matching the DUA quantities, values and shipping marks
  • Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note) evidencing departure from an EU port or airport and arrival outside the EU customs territory
  • Inward Remittance Certificate / export proceeds settlement receipt (justificante de cobro y entrada de divisas) evidencing receipt of funds via Swift LC or TT Wire into the exporter's Spanish bank account
  • Transport contract, customs forwarding instructions and Incoterms evidence (e.g., FOB or CIF)
  • Certificate of Origin (EUR.1, EUR.MED or ordinary Certificate of Origin) where required by the destination country to claim preferential or non-preferential tariff treatment

Invoices to Spanish public administrations must be issued in Facturae XML format (or an accepted interoperability format) and submitted through the General Entry Point of Invoices (Punto General de Entrada de Facturas). Invoicing software must comply with the anti-fraud requirements of Ley 11/2021 and the Verifactu Regulation (Royal Decree 1007/2023): the software and the resulting invoices must guarantee chronological integrity, generate a chained hash (hash encadenado), and display a QR code on delivered invoices; the taxable person must be able to transmit the invoicing records (Registro de Facturación) to AEAT upon demand. Under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), B2B electronic invoicing between private operators becomes mandatory once the enabling regulation enters into force, with a one-year adaptation period for enterprises exceeding EUR 8 million turnover and a two-year period for other taxpayers. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) quasi-real-time clearance regime is mandatory for enterprises with turnover above EUR 24 million and for VAT groups, requiring transmission of invoice ledger entries to AEAT within four working days of issuance or receipt; for SMEs below the threshold, SII enrolment is voluntary. Export declarations are processed electronically by AEAT's customs system (DUA / Documento Único Administrativo), but no real-time digital stamping of VAT invoices is required for export operations.

AEAT verifies export zero-ratings by cross-referencing the DUA endorsement, the Modelo 303/390 VAT summaries, the company's shipping and payment ledgers, and the Banco de España external transactions records. If the export is not conclusively proven, AEAT recharacterises the supply as a domestic taxable transaction: the output VAT at 21% is assessed, plus statutory late payment interest and a graduated penalty under Article 191 of Ley 58/2003 (LGT) of 50% to 150% of the deficient tax; defective documentation may also trigger Article 201 LGT penalties. Although no statutory 180-day repatriation deadline exists under Spanish VAT law, AEAT treats 180 days as the audit-reasonable benchmark for crediting export proceeds; longer terms require documented commercial justification, otherwise the zero-rating may be reversed and the sale treated as domestic or intra-Community. Fraudulent export schemes, including falsified DUAs, fabricated transport documents, or circular payment structures, are prosecuted as tax fraud: administrative penalties up to 150% of the tax, asset embargoes, and, where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single tax period, the criminal offence of Article 305 of the Código Penal carries imprisonment of one to five years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and disqualification. De facto administrators and managers are jointly liable under Spanish tax liability rules.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full member of the euro area; the EUR is freely convertible and capital movements are fully liberalized under Articles 63-66 TFEU and EU Regulation 2019/452. There is no exchange control approval for current account or capital account transactions. Spanish corporate profit remittance restrictions are nil for EU/EEA shareholders, while dividends to non-EU residents are subject to a reduced Spanish withholding tax rate under the applicable tax treaty where a hedge against double taxation is established. The only non-restrictive obligations are statistical reporting duties: any operation with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 (or EUR 10,000 for cash instruments) must be declared to Banco de España. Since the target entity operates in wholesale trade of dehydrated vegetables and spices, it qualifies as routine trade-related capital movement with no sectoral FDI screening trigger.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain does not impose any surrender, mandatory conversion, or deemed-repatriation obligation on export proceeds. Export receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be freely retained in domestic or overseas accounts of the Spanish SL. For statistical control, payment receipts from non-resident buyers exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction or aggregated to EUR 50,000 or more in a single calendar year must be reported via the Banco de España external transactions statistical declaration. No conversion ratio or statutory time limit applies to the holding of export proceeds.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (BdE); Foreign exchange and balance-of-payments statistical supervision is shared with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional (SGTFI) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. The regulatory framework is primarily Real Decreto 1816/1991, as amended, and Banco de España Circular 4/2022 on external transactions documentation. AML/KYC supervision is exercised by Banco de España through the Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales (SEPBLAC).

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Medium for supplementary payment rails only. Under PSD2 and Spanish Law 5/2015 on payment services, an EU-licensed electronic money institution (EDEI/EMI) can passport into Spain and provide virtual IBANs, multi-currency accounts, and low-cost FX conversion, which is useful for LATAM/US collections on the dehydrated spices trade. Legal constraints require that such EMI cannot replace a licensed credit institution for export LC confirmation, discounting, documentary credit negotiation, or provision of the statutory corporate payment account linked to the Spanish NIF/CIF that trade counterparties usually require. Banco de España Circular 1/2023 requires the EMI to apply full KYC/UBO identification and to apply the same access-to-obligations screening; an offshore, non-EU EMI must not be used as a primary operating account because such entity lacks MiFID/PSD2 pass-porting rights and creates tax-nexus and withholding-remittance risk.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident UBO structure causing beneficial ownership opacity at the 25% threshold

Root cause: Non-resident UBO structure causing beneficial ownership opacity at the 25% threshold

Defense evidence: Certified copy of the SL public deed (escritura de constitución), Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation, Spanish NIF/CIF certificate, apostilled passport copies of all UBOs, signed UBO Declaration in the Sepblac format, corporate chart showing each natural person's quota percentage, and source-of-funds evidence in the form of six-months personal bank statements and source-of-wealth declaration.
Third-party payment concentration on the supplier side, including payments routed through LATAM intermediaries or invoice factoring vehicles

Root cause: Third-party payment concentration on the supplier side, including payments routed through LATAM intermediaries or invoice factoring vehicles

Defense evidence: Original purchase orders, commercial invoices, bills of lading and weight certificates for dehydrated garlic flakes and chili pepper consignments, packing lists, marine cargo insurance policy, customs SAD/DUA export documents, and an internal counterparty due-diligence file containing the supplier's passport, trade registration, and bank letter confirming the payee is the contract beneficiary.
Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hits on any buyer or supplier name in the spice trade network

Root cause: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hits on any buyer or supplier name in the spice trade network

Defense evidence: World-Check or LexisNexis screening certificates dated within onboarding week, explanation-of-transaction narrative submitted to the Compliance Committee, country of end-user and end-use certification, and where relevant a clearance opinion from an EU sanctions lawyer demonstrating compliance with EU Regulation 269/2014 and the G7 price-cap regime if such applies.
Newly formed SL with no prior transactional history and a minimal capital balance contrary to the €3,000 SL statutory presumption

Root cause: Newly formed SL with no prior transactional history and a minimal capital balance contrary to the €3,000 SL statutory presumption

Defense evidence: Business plan covering procurement volumes, warehouse contracts, transport framework agreements, three signed purchase orders from US/LATAM/EU buyers, IAE tax census filing under epigraph equivalent to wholesale trade of food products, and an equity injection letter from the shareholders confirming the capital commitment under the Crea y Crece SL en formación sucesiva regime.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

The share capital of the Spanish SL must be disbursed by the foreign shareholder from an account held in the shareholder's own legal name via an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire; no third-party gratuitous subrogation is permitted. The MT103 reference field (tag 70) should state 'APORTACION DE CAPITAL / PRIMA DE EMISION' together with the SL's CIF/NIF and the notarial deed date. Operationally, the funds must be credited to the SL's euro-denominated operational account, and the bank should mark the credit as 'capital contribution' to facilitate the subsequent notary certificate of payment (certificado de desembolso) for Registro Mercantil filing. If the cumulative contribution exceeds EUR 50,000 in a calendar year, the SL must submit the Banco de España D-4 foreign investment statistical declaration within one month of the credit; no exchange-control permit or prior authorization is required for non-sensitive wholesale-trade activities, and no minimum capital threshold applies where the SL opts for the en formación sucesiva profile under Law 18/2022, provided the statutory restrictions on profit distribution and loss-related capital increase are observed.For the target bulk dehydrated vegetables and spices business, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for direct TT settlements and commercial letters of credit for larger or recurring LATAM and US buyers. A documentary LC must be issued by the buyer's foreign bank and advised by the Spanish SL's account bank through an MT700; once the presentation of invoice, bill of lading, phytosanitary/certificate of origin, and weight/purity certificates meets the LC terms, payment is released and booked as export proceeds via MT754/MT798. For intra-EU supplier payments, clearing should route through SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) settled in TARGET2 and EBA Clearing, while USD-denominated receipts require the Spanish bank's US correspondent account (Fedwire/CHIPS) with the SL's benefit in the SWIFT field 59; full documentation on each outgoing wire must be retained to support the EUR 50,000 statistical declaration duty and VAT export validation.Plain-vanilla EUR/USD foreign exchange forward contracts (forwards) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a local Spanish master agreement with a bank counterparty, covering underlying export receivable exposure up to 12 months tenor.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-currency exposures such as the Argentine peso or other LATAM managed-floating currencies, permissible only where the underlying export sales generate inconvertible proceeds and the NDF is entered with a licensed credit institution or authorized broker, with mandatory EMIR trade reporting to a Spanish trade repository as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold.Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/MXN) for tenor-matched long-term purchase contracts and for hedging of the fixed pricing on bulk spice supply agreements; these swaps must be collateralized under a Bank of Spain authorized ISDA CSA or local credit support annex and reported under EMIR REFIT obligations.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Medium for supplementary payment rails only. Under PSD2 and Spanish Law 5/2015 on payment services, an EU-licensed electronic money institution (EDEI/EMI) can passport into Spain and provide virtual IBANs, multi-currency accounts, and low-cost FX conversion, which is useful for LATAM/US collections on the dehydrated spices trade. Legal constraints require that such EMI cannot replace a licensed credit institution for export LC confirmation, discounting, documentary credit negotiation, or provision of the statutory corporate payment account linked to the Spanish NIF/CIF that trade counterparties usually require. Banco de España Circular 1/2023 requires the EMI to apply full KYC/UBO identification and to apply the same access-to-obligations screening; an offshore, non-EU EMI must not be used as a primary operating account because such entity lacks MiFID/PSD2 pass-porting rights and creates tax-nexus and withholding-remittance risk.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (for calendar-year accounts, approval by 30 June and deposit by 30 July). $250 USD Late filing penalties per Article 283 LSC: fines range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, depending on delay; if accounts are not deposited for 18 months, the registry closes the company's entry, preventing registration of corporate deeds and triggering administrative strike-off proceedings.
Legalization of Statutory Books (Legalización de libros) Within four months after the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year accounts, by 30 April). $90 USD Unlegalized books lack evidentiary value in commercial and tax proceedings; fines up to EUR 30,000 may be imposed; tax and accounting documents may be disregarded, leading to added assessments and surcharges.
Annual Corporation Tax Return (Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades) Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-year-end period (for calendar-year companies, 1-25 July). $0 USD Late filing surcharges of 10% plus monthly late-payment interest; after six months surcharge rises to 20%; penalties up to EUR 100,000 or more for willful non-filing; procedural restrictions on government contracts and subsidies; persistent non-filing may trigger enforcement actions but not administrative strike-off.

Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (for calendar-year accounts, approval by 30 June and deposit by 30 July).

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime (IRNR). Exemption applies to dividends paid to qualifying EU/EEA parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 5% of the Spanish SL's capital for a minimum of one year. Treaty rates may reduce the 19% statutory rate.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year entity, the filing window is 1 July through 25 July.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 20 calendar days following the end of the accumulated period. For calendar-year SLs, deadlines are 20 April (first quarter), 20 October (first nine months), and 20 December (first eleven months).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 / Casilla 00001 – NIF Tax identification number of the Spanish SL assigned by AEAT. The SL must quote its own NIF; foreign non-resident shareholders have no direct entry in this box. Any Spanish permanent establishment of a non-resident must separately register using NIF-ES with a designated representative. Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.
Box 2 / Casilla 00002 – Ejercicio Fiscal year being declared, expressed as a four-digit tax period. Use the calendar fiscal year unless an alternate tax period was approved by AEAT; foreign ownership does not alter the entity's fiscal period. Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.
Box 108 / Casilla 00108 – Resultado contable Net accounting profit or loss for the year before corporate income tax, determined under Spanish GAAP. The SL reports its full worldwide accounting result. A non-resident parent's consolidation entries or foreign tax provisions are excluded from this box. Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.
Box 115 / Casilla 00115 – Base imponible Taxable base after statutory adjustments, including exemption and participation-relief rules, book-tax differences, and prior-year loss offset. Claim the participation exemption (Art. 21 LIS) here only if the SL's qualifying holding in a non-resident affiliate meets the shareholding and holding-period requirements. Attach supporting parent company ownership details. Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.
Box 565 / Casilla 00565 – Líquido a ingresar / cantidad a devolver Final tax due after quarterly prepayments, withholdings and credits, or the amount refundable. If the SL paid dividends, royalties or interest to a non-resident, related withholding tax payments must be made under separate forms (Modelo 123/210/216) and are reconciled through this box. Late filing without prior administrative demand triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the tax administration issues an assessment after the filing deadline, penalties of 50% to 100% of the unpaid amount may be imposed, together with interest. A minimum fixed fine of EUR 200 applies for incomplete or incorrect returns.
Line 1 / Casilla 00001 – Ejercicio Tax year for which the prepayment is made. Same fiscal year as Modelo 200; non-resident shareholders have no separate filing obligation in this form. Late or omitted Modelo 202 payments are subject to the same graduated surcharge regime under Article 27 LGT, enforced collection in default cases, and daily late-payment interest; failure to file the return itself carries an additional fixed penalty of EUR 200.
Line 2 / Casilla 00002 – Representante Must be marked when the filing is made by a tax representative. For a non-resident parent or agent, only when the Spanish SL is represented by an appointed tax representative. Late or omitted Modelo 202 payments are subject to the same graduated surcharge regime under Article 27 LGT, enforced collection in default cases, and daily late-payment interest; failure to file the return itself carries an additional fixed penalty of EUR 200.
Line 3 / Casilla 00003 – Cuota resultante Prepayment amount calculated on the accumulated taxable base using the simplified or rejoinder methodology. Foreign shareholders must recognise this as a prepayment of the SL's final corporate tax; it is not a tax on the parent company. Late or omitted Modelo 202 payments are subject to the same graduated surcharge regime under Article 27 LGT, enforced collection in default cases, and daily late-payment interest; failure to file the return itself carries an additional fixed penalty of EUR 200.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Mandatory Local File and Modelo 232 annual related-party reporting are triggered when the aggregate amount of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 in a fiscal year. A Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated worldwide net turnover reaches EUR 75 million. Transactions with tax-haven jurisdictions are subject to lower de minimis thresholds and must always be documented.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not apply an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulation; instead, it applies the OECD-aligned substance-over-form doctrine through Article 15 LIS (anti-abuse), Article 100 LGT (fraud of law), and the CFC rules of Article 100 LIS. A Spanish SL engaged in bulk dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper export must maintain demonstrable local substance: real office or warehouse, locally resident management, operational contracts, payroll, business correspondence, financial accounts, and commercial risk. Beginning January 2019, letterbox companies lacking economic substance may be disregarded, income re-attributed, and treaty benefits denied where management and control are effectively exercised abroad.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / Delito Fiscal

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount, loss of subsidies and public procurement rights, and public conviction disclosure. The AEAT additionally imposes a civil tax penalty of 50%–100% of the unpaid tax plus late-payment interest.

Director personal liability: Any director who participates, orders, consents, or negligently fails to supervise the evasion is criminally responsible. Directors may be personally imprisoned and ordered to pay civil restitution; the corporate veil is pierced to attach personal assets, and travel bans, passport surrender, and seizure of director bank accounts may be imposed during criminal investigation.
Sham / Artificial Shell (Letterbox) Structure

Statutory sanction: AEAT recharacterises the arrangement under the general French anti-abuse doctrine, applies CF, and detrives treaty benefits; the taxable base is recalculated at the 25% corporate rate, plus a 50% penalty, late interest, and additional surcharges. The arrangement may be re-qualified as a permanent establishment of the foreign entity, triggering additional non-resident taxation.

Director personal liability: Directors who allow the company to function as a pure shell are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts under Articles 42.2 and 43 LGT. Liability extension includes personal bank accounts, vehicles, and real property; criminal proceedings may result in imprisonment for tax evasion, and a travel ban can be issued to secure the director's presence.
Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure

Statutory sanction: Failure to provide required TP documentation triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 1,500 per omitted or inaccurate data item, with a minimum penalty of EUR 5,000. If the absence of documentation prevents the AEAT from confirming the arm's-length result, an additional tax adjustment is made with a 50% surcharge on the tax difference. Recidivism elevates the sanction.

Director personal liability: The director who signs the Modelo 200 or who knowingly fails to produce TP evidence can be declared jointly liable for the corporate tax adjustment under Article 42.2 LGT. In serious cases of false documentation, criminal liability for falsification of accounts or fraud may be pursued, with possible imprisonment and travel restrictions.
AML / Anti-Money Laundering Violations

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines under Law 10/2010: minor infractions up to EUR 60,000, serious infractions from EUR 60,000 to EUR 150,000, and very serious infractions from EUR 150,000 up to EUR 5,000,000. Separate tax penalties and seizure of undeclared cash are imposed for concurrent tax offences.

Director personal liability: Directors of the Spanish SL are 'obliged subjects' under Spanish AMLA. Directors who personally breach KYC, registration, or reporting duties are individually fined. Criminal money-laundering convictions under Article 301 of the Criminal Code carry 6 months to 6 years imprisonment and confiscation of assets; travel bans and passport suspension are commonly ordered.
